entities.text: High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Navin Chawla
 Order
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

2. This petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short,
'Cr.P.C.') seeking quashing of FIR No.423/2018 registered at Police Station: Farsh Bazar, Shahdara District, Delhi, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short, 'IPC'), along with all other proceedings arising therefrom, on the basis of a settlement.
3. Issue notice.
4. Notice is accepted by Mr. Shoaib Haider, learned APP.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the subject FIR was an offshoot of the matrimonial discord between the parties, that is, the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no. 2.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the parties, that is, the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2, have amicably settled all their, inter se, disputes before the Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi and have entered into a Settlement dated 07.06.2022.

entities.text: Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
7. He submits that pursuant to the abovementioned settlement, the parties have also been granted a Decree of Divorce by mutual consent dated 14.11.2022 passed by the learned Principal Judge,
Family Court, Shahdara District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.

entities.text:
Principal Judge,
Family Court, Shahdara District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
entities.label: JUDGE

sentences.text: 8. The respondent no.2 is personally present in Court and has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer (IO).
She submits that all the amounts in terms of the settlement have been received by her.
She states that as the matter has been amicably settled, she does not wish to pursue her complaint.
9. The respondent no.2 reaffirms that she has settled all the disputes with the petitioners out of her own free will and without any coercion.
She submits that she has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.
10. I have perused the contents of the FIR and also the settlement between the parties.

11. As the disputes between the parties arose out of a matrimonial relationship, and now the same have been amicably settled, Decree of Divorce has also been granted to the parties pursuant to the settlement, and also looking into the nature of the allegations made in the complaint, in my opinion,
no useful purpose would be served in keeping the FIR alive.
In fact, it would rather create further acrimony
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 01/06/2024 at 01:20:49 between the parties and will be an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.

12. Guided by the principles enunciated by the Supreme Court in its judgments in Jitendra Raghuvanshi v. Babita Raghuvanshi, (2013) 4 SCC 58; Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303; Parbatbhai Aahir @ Parbatbhai Bhimsinbhai Karmur & Ors. v. State of Gujarat & Ors., (2017) 9 SCC 641; and, State of Haryana & Ors. v. Bhajan Lal & Ors., 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, this Court deems it appropriate, in the interest of justice, to exercise its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. to quash the FIR and all the proceedings emanating therefrom.

FIR No.423/2018 registered at Police Station: Farsh Bazar,
Shahdara District, Delhi, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom against the petitioners are quashed.
